proctor-prediction.notes: v2 best: XGBoost + SHAP interaction features (NMAE=0.2548). v3: PINN with ZAV saturation + air-voids physics loss; ablation over λ_ZAV ∈ {0,0.5,1,5,10} + ensemble with XGBoost. Requires KMP_DUPLICATE_LIB_OK=TRUE; uses MPS (Apple Silicon). v5 plan added 2026-07-02: SINDy sparse symbolic feature discovery + SHAP-guided refinement (materializing v2's redundant-pair/interaction findings) + GBM/PINN stacked ensemble. Target: beat v1's 0.2431 CV NMAE. v5 implemented 2026-07-02: SINDy (STLSQ static sparse symbolic regression, repurposed from dynamical-systems use) discovered 21 nonlinear feature terms; SHAP refinement dropped 11 redundant raw/log PSD cols and materialized 10 interaction product features (acting on v2 findings that were never applied); Optuna-tuned XGBoost (0.2441) blended 0.8/0.2 with a PINN diversity model (0.2776 alone) beat both individually and the Ridge-meta-learner alternative (0.2575): final CV NMAE 0.2410, new best. Required pinning OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 etc. before importing xgboost/lightgbm/shap/torch together in one process -- otherwise the run deadlocks at PINN training (first version to combine GBM and PINN in a single kernel). Updated 2026-07-02 15:15 to reuse helper_functions.py (calc_satline, get_missing_data_report) per user request; verified mathematically behavior-neutral (calc_satline is the identical ZAV formula, incl. on torch tensors) and re-validated end-to-end -- CV NMAE 0.2420, still beats v1. load_and_summarize_data was tried but doesn't fit this repo's split data/ + root sample_submission.csv layout, so skipped.
